title: OS.read_buffer_from_stdin() returns the whole buffer filled with old memory on Windows
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]

### System information

Windows 11 build 26200, Godot v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] (running --headless)

### Issue description

I'm working on a small headless tool for my game where a python script plays the game by sending moves over stdin.

`read_string_from_stdin` strips the newlines, so a read that only got a `\n` comes back as `""`, same as when the pipe closes. The docs say to use `read_buffer_from_stdin` for unprocessed data, so I switched to it, and noticed a strange potential bug?

It seems that, at least on Windows, `read_buffer_from_stdin` always hands back the full `buffer_size`, no matter how much was actually read, and whatever comes after the data is old memory.

In my case I sent the text/bytes `AB\n`, calling it like this (this is the MRP's script; the `0xAA` part is only there to see whether old memory shows up):

```gdscript
print("stdin type: %d" % OS.get_stdin_type())
var canary := PackedByteArray()
canary.resize(64)
canary.fill(0xAA)
canary = PackedByteArray() # freed right before the reads
for i in 4:
	var got := OS.read_buffer_from_stdin(64)
	print("read %d: size %d: %s" % [i + 1, got.size(), got.hex_encode()])
	if got.is_empty():
		break

```

and got 64 bytes back.

So to recap:

**What I send** (3 bytes through a pipe):

```
41 42 0a                      "AB\n"

```

**What I expect** (what the docs describe, and what the Linux/macOS code does):

```
read 1 -> 3 bytes:   41 42 0a
read 2 -> 0 bytes    (pipe closed)

```

**What I get on Windows:**

```
read 1 -> 64 bytes:  41 42 0a 00 74 00 00 00 64 00 00 00 69 00 00 00 6e 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 74 00 00 00 79 00 00 00 70 00 00 00 65 00 00 00 3a 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 33 00 00 00 0a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
read 2 -> 0 bytes

```

Which does show my `AB\n`... but then a whole bunch of data I never asked for. The 64-byte size happens every single time I've tried it; what's in the extra 61 bytes varies.

Mostly it's zeros, but in one run it was the line my script printed just before the read. Read 4 bytes at a time (UTF-32, which is how Godot stores a String), `74 00 00 00` is `t`, `64 00 00 00` is `d`, and so on, spelling `tdin type: 3\n`, with the `s` overwritten by my `AB\n`.

And it gets worse if `stdin` is a file.  
After EOF it never returns an empty array and just keeps giving back 64 bytes, so essentially the expectation of "read until empty" never happens and the loop never ends. The docs say a file read returns "a specific amount of data (or less if end-of-file is reached)".

And what comes back after EOF is my own script's earlier `print()` lines, as if they were input. Same 3 bytes, from a file this time, on 4.7:

```
read 1 -> 64 bytes:  41 42 0a 00 74 00 00 00 64 00 00 00 ...   "AB\n", then "tdin type: 2\n"
read 2 -> 64 bytes:  73 00 00 00 74 00 00 00 64 00 00 00 ...   "stdin type: 2"
read 3 -> 64 bytes:  72 00 00 00 65 00 00 00 61 00 00 00 ...   "read 2: size 64:"
read 4 -> 64 bytes:  72 00 00 00 65 00 00 00 61 00 00 00 ...   "read 1: size 64:"

```

Read 3 is the line my script printed after read 2, and read 4 the one it printed after read 1. In another run, read 3 came back as 64 bytes of `aa`, which is the buffer my script filled with `0xAA` and freed right before reading. 4.7.2 does the same.

From what I could find from a combination of manual searching + some ai help: `OS_Windows::get_stdin_buffer()` never uses the `count` from `ReadFile()` and returns the whole resized vector:  
[os_windows.cpp#L2109](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7-stable/platform/windows/os_windows.cpp#L2109-L2118).  
The Unix version does `data.resize(sz)` and returns empty when nothing was read: [os_unix.cpp#L208](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7-stable/drivers/unix/os_unix.cpp#L208-L217).

And Windows' `get_stdin_string()` uses `count` too, so I assume it's just a missing resize?

```cpp
if (ReadFile(GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE), data.ptrw(), data.size(), &count, nullptr) && count > 0) {
	data.resize(count);
	return data;
}
return PackedByteArray();

```

For now I'm reading 1 byte at a time, which works but it's not exactly ideal for automating stdin testing.

### Steps to reproduce

1.  Unzip the MRP and import it once: `godot --headless --path . --import` (any Godot 4.6+ binary).
2.  Pipe case: `python drive.py pipe path/to/Godot_v4.x-stable_win64_console.exe`. Expected `read 1: size 3`, then `read 2: size 0`; actual `read 1: size 64`.
3.  File case: `python drive.py file path/to/Godot_v4.x-stable_win64_console.exe`. Expected `read 1: size 3`, then `read 2: size 0`; actual: all four reads are size 64.

Use the `_console.exe` build so its output reaches the script. Leave out the path to use `godot` from the PATH.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[stdin_buffer_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33217682/stdin_buffer_mrp.zip)
